bifrost: springboard/core/src/sha256.rs (bifrost_core::sha256), springboard/src/keychain.rs (HMAC-SHA256, ChaCha20, encrypt-then-MAC), springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (secret storage only)
summary: BifrOSt has SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256 and ChaCha20 inside the shell, used only to protect the keychain file and to verify updates and backups. Apps get no hashing, cipher, signature, key agreement or typed key API; the SDK keychain stores opaque secret bytes. Most of CryptoKit (SHA-2 384/512, SHA-3, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Curve25519, NIST curves, HPKE, HKDF, post-quantum KEM and signatures, Secure Enclave) has no counterpart.

features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. Wave 4 (w4-apple-cryptokit, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. SHA-256 only, in the shell's core crate; no SDK type, no SHA-384 or SHA-512, no HashFunction protocol

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 4 (w4-apple-cryptokit, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no SHA-3 implementation in springboard/

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 4 (w4-apple-cryptokit, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. HMAC-SHA256 is private to the keychain module; no SymmetricKey type and no HMAC API for apps

RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a 32-byte ChaChaPolyKey that seals to nonce, ciphertext and tag and opens only on a matching tag; tested headless against the RFC section 2.5.2 and 2.8.2 vectors in tests/parity_sdk-rest-05.rs. Gap: the keychain still uses its own HMAC-SHA256 encrypt-then-MAC (keychain.rs seal_with and open_box), and the AEAD is not verified on Midget.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 10 tests. Wave 6 (b16, main): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on Midget. no AES in springboard/; the noVNC JavaScript under springboard/apps/remote is a web client and not used by apps
verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 16 tests. derives per-app subkeys with HMAC from a master key; this is an ad hoc construction, not HKDF, and is not exposed to apps

features.feature: Public-key signatures (Curve25519 Ed25519, P256, P384, P521)
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 12 tests. Curve25519.Signing (Ed25519, RFC 8032) done as a pure model with host unit tests: PrivateKey, PublicKey, CryptoKitError; not yet tested on Midget. P256, P384 and P521 are still missing

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 4 (theme-03, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no Diffie-Hellman or X25519 in springboard/

Base mode of RFC 9180 with DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256 and AES-128-GCM, with sealing, opening and exporter tests in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-gaps-01.rs. Gap: no PSK or authenticated modes, no other KEM or AEAD suites, and no SDK type for the HPKE key protocols, so apps cannot reach it yet.

features.feature: Post-quantum KEM and signatures (ML-KEM, X-Wing, ML-DSA)
features.apple: MLKEM768, MLKEM1024, XWingMLKEM768X25519, KEM, KEMPrivateKey, KEMPublicKey, MLDSA65, MLDSA87
features.bifrost: springboard/core/src/mlkem.rs (ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024: NTT, CBD and SampleNTT sampling, Compress, K-PKE, KeyGen/Encaps/Decaps with implicit rejection and the FIPS 203 key checks; tests mlkem::tests::*), springboard/core/src/sha3.rs (Shake: SHAKE128/256 XOF; tests shake_*), springboard/sdk/src/kem.rs (bifrost_app::kem: DecapsulationKey, EncapsulationKey, Variant; tests in kem::tests), springboard/core/src/mldsa.rs (ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87: NTT, Power2Round, Decompose, hints, bit packings, SampleInBall, KeyGen/Sign/Verify with the rejection loop, pure interface with context; tests in mldsa::tests), springboard/sdk/src/signature_pq.rs (bifrost_app::signature_pq: PrivateKey, PublicKey, Variant; tests in signature_pq::tests)
features.note: ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024 are implemented from FIPS 203 with a pure model; the SDK draws the seeds from the kernel pool. ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 are implemented from FIPS 204 (sign, verify, deterministic and hedged signing, context strings); the SDK draws the signing randomness from the pool. Not checked: the official FIPS 203 and FIPS 204 known-answer vectors are not in the repo, so the tests check lengths, NTT round trips and multiplication, codecs, round trips, implicit rejection and the failure cases only; nothing is verified against other implementations, and the row is not parity until the vectors pass and it runs on Midget. Still missing for this row: X-Wing (XWingMLKEM768X25519), and the KEM and KEMPublicKey type shapes.

features.feature: Typed key storage in the keychain
features.apple: CryptoKit keys stored as keychain items (sample: Storing CryptoKit Keys in the Keychain)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (add, get, update, delete); springboard/sdk/src/keychain_keys.rs (encode, decode, add, update, decode_reply); springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-01d.rs; springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-41.rs
features.note: Typed keys are stored as a kind-tagged record in one keychain item, and the record is checked headless on read: wrong magic, unknown kind and bad key length are refused. Gap: there are no key references, and keys are not reachable from apps outside the keychain calls; the keychain round trip needs the shell on Midget.
Apple hardware. The keychain comments say no TPM or login-password key source exists yet (springboard/src/keychain.rs header), so a hardware key source would be a new gap, not a port

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 10 tests. Wave 5 (w5-apple-cryptokit, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. the shell has no MD5 or SHA-1; only the noVNC web client has MD5
App Store Connect metadata; BifrOSt's PC App Store has no equivalent key in its manifest format

gaps: No app-facing SDK API for any hashing, cipher, MAC or signature primitive; apps can only store opaque secrets
SHA-2 is only SHA-256 and is not exposed; SHA-384, SHA-512 and SHA-3 are missing
No AES-GCM and no ChaCha20-Poly1305 with Poly1305; the shell's ChaCha20 is internal and paired with HMAC instead
No asymmetric crypto: Ed25519, X25519 and NIST curve signatures or key agreement
No HKDF, HPKE or post-quantum KEM and signatures
No typed key objects (SymmetricKey, key references) in the keychain API
No hardware-backed key source (Secure Enclave or TPM)
